sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Optivalue Tek is a small IT integration, consulting and staffing business attempting a more capital-intensive software, licensed anti-drone and hardware expansion. Reported FY26 revenue of₹90.74 crore and several large announced contracts create a plausible growth story; they do not yet establish a cash-generating compounder. The decisive risk is the unreconciled audit-evidence conflict over₹59.87 crore receivables and approximately₹14 crore unbilled revenue, compounded by negative operating cash and object-restricted IPO funds. Preserve the favorable facts: related advances are stated to have been repaid with interest, annual audit/IFC opinions are unmodified, and the annual audit describes alternative collection checks. Those facts do not quantify a cure.

At the verified 19 October close₹218.40, market capitalization is₹511.30 crore. Ordinary expected return, fair entry price and all three composite scores are NS, with G 2/G 3 Hold and no numerical ranking. This is an unresolved special-situation / execution watchlist, not a verified compounder or a fresh-entry recommendation. Even an explicitly optimistic, funded early-repayment repair model gives -1.6% annualized return at the quoted price and a conditional 15% hurdle price₹100.03; that number is not a buying recommendation while reliability and current funding remain unknown. Evidence of collected opening balances, authorized recoveries, usable funding and profitable product delivery would matter more than another headline order.

G 2 Hold independently excludes all rankings. R/D/P stay NS rather than borrowing an attractive return from an early-repayment or rescue counterfactual.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The original business supplies IT consulting, systems integration, digital engineering, staffing and project delivery, frequently through system integrators rather than directly to the ultimate government customer. Revenue is recognized against delivered services or project obligations; cash depends on customer acceptance, invoicing and collection. Nonexclusive work orders and staff-hour deployment are materially different from subscription software revenue. FY26 professional-consultancy revenue₹90.3866 crore dwarfs goods revenue₹.3521 crore. Foreign revenue₹11.7148 crore is 12.91% of FY26 sales, versus₹1.2304 crore a year earlier. The company reports one IT-consultancy segment; selecting geography in an exchange form does not create audited product-segment profitability.

The new direction adds an acquired software/licence asset, capitalized in-house development and defence/drone products. The₹375 crore five-year Citrix Project Development Consultant LLC announcement is support-staff work at USD 16/hour for 225+staff, not demonstrated Saa SARR or evidence of affiliation with the similarly named global software vendor. The₹64 crore Aaroosha project is a finite website ecosystem engagement, replacing₹16.25 crore earlier scope. Nano-drone PO₹20.70 crore is milestone-dependent. The₹70 crore Aerial IQ announcement is a tentative LOI, not a firm contract. Product certification, manufacturing/vendor capacity, warranties, licences and post-delivery collections introduce demands not established by historic consulting margins. No acquired corporate revenue is identified; buying a licence and hiring for a new contract are reinvestment, not a proven existing moat.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Evidence supports useful implementation experience, customer relationships and integration capability, but not durable pricing power. RHP contracts are generally nonexclusive and largely with system integrators; contracts can be project-specific and customer concentration is high. FY25 top 10 customer revenue₹38.0457 crore is 67.84% of sales. The top 5 table prints 45.61%, but₹25.8741 crore divided by₹56.0785 crore is 46.14%;FY24 top 10 amount likewise does not exactly match its printed percentage. The raw amounts and discrepancies are retained rather than polished into artificial precision. These relationships may help win work but customers retain meaningful bargaining power and payment control.

FY25 had 70 full-time and 70–80 contract staff, with 54.68% reported attrition. A new 225+staff international commitment therefore requires substantial recruitment, training, supervision and payroll before realizing a five-year headline. Product pilot acceptance is a qualification milestone, not evidence of exclusive intellectual property, installed-base lock-in, recurring maintenance pricing or after-sales profitability. Licence dependence and technology obsolescence can transfer value to licensors and vendors. RHP peers Dev Information Technology and Euphoria Infotech are only qualitative reference points: scale, consolidation and product mix differ, and prospectus peer/KPI inconsistencies make unverified quoted multiples inappropriate anchors. MOAT 4 recognizes a functioning but contestable business. Failure modes are price competition, staff turnover, intermediary concentration and product procurement delays, not an assumed collapse of a nonexistent subscription franchise.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The preferred five-year organic CAGR cannot be calculated because FY21 is absent: five annual observations FY22–26 span four intervals. The preselected fallback is FY23–26, three comparable reported annual intervals,32.69% CAGR;FY22–26 four-interval 32.84% is supplementary. No consolidation acquisition explains the jump, and service revenue grows 76.26% in FY26 while hardware trading falls. Nevertheless price/volume cohorts and collected recurring customer revenue are undisclosed, and the material audit-evidence limitation means exact underlying organic expansion is not identified. Consequently these are reported growth diagnostics and REV remains NS.

Revenue declines in FY24 before rebounding; recomputing from₹38.8432 crore to₹36.5604 crore gives−5.88%, not an inconsistent prospectus narrative percentage. FY26 H 1 revenue₹30.4872 crore and H 2₹60.2515 crore show a strong reported exit trajectory, but H 2 PAT₹6.5365 crore is below H 1₹7.2260 crore. There is no automatic upgrade from a single exceptionally large order or uncollected half-year. FY26 annual revenue increment₹34.6603 crore is economically substantial relative to the₹38.8432 crore FY23 base, but conversion and unit margins determine whether that growth creates owner value.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible opportunity consists of staff deployment, finite project work and products requiring new capabilities. There is no useful top-down TAM shortcut. Conditional Base annual revenue buckets FY27–32 are legacy 95/104/112/120/127/134, international 25/48/54/56/56/18, website 18/27/0/0/0/0, and hardware 8/16/20/24/29/34 crore. These are analyst assumptions below tax-inclusive order headlines, not company guidance. International work starts July 2026 and ends July 2031; website recognizes₹45 crore net once within the finite contract. The tentative₹70 crore LOI contributes zero automatic sales. Forecast hardware beyond the first disclosed PO still requires fresh wins. At 225 staff×USD 16×2,080 hours×₹85/USD, illustrative annual billing is₹63.648 crore before tax, demonstrating why utilization and exchange rates matter to a₹75 crore gross yearly headline.

Future margins charge shared corporate 1.5% and recurring R&D 3% of sales separately from direct segment contribution. Remaining platform completion₹5.77 crore is additionally expensed overtwo years and funded only from its eligible IPO object; branch/hardware₹2.88 crore is incremental tangible cash capex. Existing₹11.2925 crore licence amortizes overfour productive years and requires a modeled cash replacement in July 2030. Existing software begins a five-year assumed amortization only after completion; future R&D does not disappear at terminal value. The exact dated cash model retains old tax/statutory/benefit liabilities, term debt, leases and working-capital needs; neither retained earnings nor a restricted FD is treated as a cost-free funding line.

Historical R&D-expensed incremental NOPAT/IC is 9.87% for FY23–26 and 4.38% for FY24–26, below the 12–18% cost-of-capital reference range, versus 45.58% before the recent capital shift. These are useful warning diagnostics, not project returns or proof of permanent value destruction. Missing confirmation and commissioning cohorts leave CAP NS. GQS cannot be finalized, and CASH 2 independently caps any eventual score at 5 until persistent realization improves. Conservative Base has a modeled peak shortfall₹0.98 crore before entry under the latest-date repayment assumption; a differently timed actual receipt could change that path, which is precisely why it is not declared an observed default.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters retain 64.07% after an all-fresh IPO. Alignment through retained ownership is helpful but not sufficient. Related funding is particularly material: the detailed note gives₹2.7539 crore due from the managing director after a cancelled IT-asset procurement and₹5.3886 crore from Winghover including accrued interest, total₹8.1425 crore. The annual auditor says these were recovered with interest after the balance date. This substantially weakens a simple permanent-diversion allegation; it does not establish authorization at the time, the exact receipt date or a clean reconciliation of differing gross movement amounts. The main legal report records Section 185 noncompliance; CARO says 185/186 complied. Both must remain visible.

The monitoring history is also mixed. The prior agency was terminated and Acuite reports show changes in expense/GST treatment and object use. The H 2 headline says no deviation, but limitations and inability to ascertain utilization are not cured by that headline. CARO reports no fraud noticed and no default/wilful-defaulter status; those are important boundaries. A clean IFC opinion coexists with Excel-based timesheets without system controls, a recommendation for stronger supplier/customer agreements and no internal-audit report supplied to the statutory auditor. An internal auditor appointment is not the same as an available completed report. The secretarial annexure gives generally compliant findings with unquantified filing delays, excludes financial-record correctness and offers no viability assurance. The October independent-director resignation gives personal/travel reasons and is not treated as evidence of misconduct. No conclusion about audit-trail tampering is invented from an omitted explicit assessment.

sections.text:
All amounts below are₹ crore exceptper-share ratios, shares anddays. Latest FY26 comparatives govern minor FY25 reclassifications; RHP FY23–25 supersedes older DRHP cash-flow presentation, particularly overdraft classifications. FY22 is disclosed separately as less comparable. FY25 PAT₹12.1390 crore must not be confused with₹12.1860 crore total comprehensive income. FY26 reported weighted EPS₹6.66 is not current-share EPS₹5.8785. Current ownership uses 23,411,400 shares for every valuation, not a pre-IPO denominator.

The FY26 earnings bridge starts at operating EBIT₹17.3398 crore, excluding all₹1.4866 crore other income, of which₹1.3879 crore is FD interest. Expense₹6.7324 crore capitalized development costs and add back₹.1145 crore IPO expense to get economic recurring EBIT₹10.7219 crore. A prospective full-year licence charge₹2.823125 crore reduces that run-rate illustration to₹7.898775 crore, not an assertion that FY26 no-sale amortization was illegal. Tax 25.17% is an analytical rate; actual current/prior/deferred effects remain in the primary table. FY26 gross employee and subcontract costs were₹11.4072 and₹65.5874 crore before capitalization. Capitalized R&D must be removed consistently from both earnings and invested capital for an expensed basis.

Cash is much weaker than profit. FY26 reported CFO−₹11.8871 crore includes advances−₹13.6867 crore, receivables−₹42.8218 crore and supplier financing+₹31.8917 crore. The cash-flow receivable movement differs slightly from balance-sheet movement and is preserved, not forced. Adding the full advance movement back would produce only₹1.7996 crore,13.08% of PAT, and would wrongly assume all advances were nonoperating. Adding only known incremental related advances₹7.6720 crore still leaves CFO−₹4.2151 crore. Capex is investing cash and cannot explain negative CFO. Reported FCF is CFO minus reported cash capex, with no artificial ROU cash correction.

Year-end billed receivable days and contract-asset days are separately computed; average DSO uses opening/closing billed receivables and exact fiscal days. Trade-payable days use expensed subcontract/material cost as a proxy, so capitalization and timing limit comparability. Note 15 ageing totals differ from face payables; no ECLcharge is disclosed despite the May inability to evidence recoverability. Grossageing mostly under 6 months does not substitute for customer confirmations or collections.

The operating IC bridge excludes cash, FD s, DTA, TDS, accrued interest and known related advances; old operating statutory/benefit balances reduce historical IC. FY25 related-advance versus related-loan classification remains unresolved, so the primary bridge does not invent a deduction; a₹.4705 crore sensitivity cannot explain the FY26 capital step-up. Starting model ONWC₹47.9926 crore equals₹46.0342 crore accounting IC lessfixed assets plus₹1.9646 crore old statutory/benefit liabilities separately paid, less₹.0062 crore government advance. This is a transparent reclassification, not a cash plug. The asset bridge reconciles cumulative capex−DA−fixed-asset change to₹.0060 crore in FY23–26; the cash flow treatment of ROU additions still needs explanation. Debt/leases, current tax₹4.1001 crore and other old dues are separately modeled. The GST note₹.1823 crore contingent amount differs from CARO₹.1192 crore; no assumed paid amount is hidden in CFO.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations

The primary method is a finite-life, sector-linked cash-funding model plus terminal EV/recurring EBIT, not a generic sales multiple or a perpetual₹375 crore order book. The market snapshot is₹511.305 crore equity value,37.15× FY26 PAT,5.56× book and₹519.955 crore conservative EV including debt/leases and only₹.4928 crore apparently unrestricted Marchbank cash. Gross-cash EV₹497.688 crore is a diagnostic that ignores deposit restrictions, not a safer valuation. Reportedoperating EBIT multiple is 29.99×; R&D-expensed EBIT multiple 48.49×. Company-reported weighted EPS₹6.66 is not the current-share denominator. These ratios combine an Octoberprice with Marchaccounts and are not verified October EV.

Ordinary Bear/Base/Bull returns and entry prices are null because their pre-entry funding paths fail under a conservative May 28 receipt bound and current liquidity is not established. Themodel does not assert that the company actually defaulted in April: the precise related repayment date, payment timing and earlier collections are unknown. It exposes the information needed to establish survivability. A separate repair case assumes all₹8.1425 crore related money was received 1 April 2026, not a documented date, and permits premature IPO FD encashment only against eligible spending. This is not a rescue. Under that favorable timing,18× forward recurring EBIT yields -1.6% annualized return and₹100.03 conditional 15% entry price. The large discount to₹218.40 cannot cure G 2 or G 3 and is not an executable buy threshold.

Monthly/dately cash starts 31 March 2026 with₹.4928 crore free bank cash, not₹22.7589 crore gross cash/deposits. The initial IPO allocation 19.09 is ringfenced by development 5.77, branch 1.31, hardware 1.57, WC 5.55 and general corporate 4.89; the published.01 rounding difference is removed from GCP. Unallocated.0161 bank-note difference stays restricted. The conditional case may redeem deposits for eligible costs; the delayed FD case allows only₹1.09 crore starting IPO cash before March 2027. Non IPO FD₹3.16 crore is not available until assumed March 2028. Oldtax, statutory, CSR, audit and gratuity are paid once; related receipts and deposit release occur once. No unused banklimit, new debt or unfunded cash plug is supplied. Floor₹.25 crore before entry and₹1 crore thereafter is a thin analyst minimum; larger floors are tested. Cash before dated receipts is also tested, so a late receipt cannot erase an earlier gap. Period-end tests still cannot prove intra-period bank liquidity.

The FY32 annual budget is not a full year of holding-period cash: only through 20 October 2031 is realized. International support begins July 2026 and stops July 2031; website work ends October 2027. Terminal EV uses forward recurring legacy/hardware EBIT with expired work excluded entirely, rather than annualizing the remaining contract or capitalizing TTMwindfall. TTMmetrics are separately disclosed. Existing software amortization starts 1 April 2028 after modeled completion and continues five years; this commissioning date is an assumption. Licence amortization and₹11.2925 crore July 2030 replacement continue the economic cost. Recurring R&D, corporate cost and replacement rent remain in terminal earnings. Forecast operating WC is retained; no automatic release for expired contracts is valued. Terminalcash is signed free cash less 5% recurring sales reserve, not max(cash,0); debt and leases are deducted. No operating-property bonus, NCI or dividends are assumed.

Multiples 10–26×and margin±3 points are scenario assumptions, not claimed observed peer fair values. There are 56 complete sensitivity rows, including DSO/DPO, capex/R&D, minimum cash, restricted FD access, late RPT repayment and receivable collection loss. At the repair-case economics, the 15% hurdle requires approximately 44.53×exit recurring EBIT. A funded bracketed growth root requires legacy IT growth 24.6% annually while the other finite contract budgets remain fixed. Root residuals and brackets are exposed; no finite sign-changing funded bracket means NS, not an extrapolated answer.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest adverse case is not simply slower IT growth. Billing or collection problems absorb cash while salaries, subcontractors, statutory dues and product commitments require payment; suppliers reduce extended credit just as tax-restricted or IPO-earmarked deposits cannot cover arbitrary uses. The company may then require costly new capital or lose projects. A large tax-inclusive order can worsen this if early mobilization precedes customer acceptance. A finite staffing contract or website project cannot support a perpetual valuation after expiry. Product amortization, warranties, licence renewal and R&D can consume accounting margins even when recognized sales rise.

Bear assumptions reduce legacy and new contract realization, compress contribution margins 5 points, hold DSO 240 days/unbilled 75 days and shorten payable credit to 75 days. Ten-percent loss of old receivable realization is modeled as missing collection, not an additional cash payment plus a duplicate asset write-off. The non-rescue path peaks at₹34.01 crore unfunded need and no finite investable return is presented. Even the more favorable Base fails an earlycash floor under latest-date repayment timing. This is a conditional stress result, not proof of historical insolvency. Permanent loss can arise through dilution, creditor seniority, client loss or an exit multiple that does not capitalize temporary work. A zero or deeply negative owner outcome is possible in an unfinanced failure, but no unsupported exact bankruptcy recovery is assigned.

The strongest favorable counterargument is material: annual audit procedures include subsequent-realization checks, related money is stated to have been returned with interest, most receivables fall in relatively recent ageing buckets, and disclosed contracts could absorb existing capacity. If complete bank/customer evidence demonstrates prompt receipts and unrestricted funding, the conservative path may be too harsh. That counterargument must be tested with balances and cash rather than dismissed or assumed. The thesis-break variable is funded, collected recurring operating profit after R&D and licence costs, not a press-release order total.

sections.text:
A fivefold share price in this horizon requires approximately 38% annualized ownership return; tenfold requires 58.5%. Neither follows from the₹375 crore five-year gross contract, a₹70 crore tentative LOI or a one-off equity-funded asset step-up. At an 18×EBIT terminal multiple, ignoring net cash/debt for a clean scale test,5×equity value requires₹142.03 crore recurring EBIT and 10×requires₹284.06 crore. At 15% EBIT margin these imply₹946.86 crore and₹1,893.72 crore recurring annual sales, versus FY26₹90.74 crore and normalized EBIT₹10.72 crore. The funded repair case forward recurring revenue₹168 crore is nowhere near those scales.

This is a feasibility hurdle, not a prediction or a claimed upper limit. Higher sustainable margins or multiples reduce required sales, but the multiple must survive finite-contract expiry and evidence quality; funding and dilution increase what the original owner must achieve. sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitoring is evidence-triggered rather than a promise of price tracking or automatic trading. The next meaningful review should use results covering post-IPO/current contract operations, updated source documents and an explicit opening-to-closing cash bridge. Every gate has a specific evidentiary cure; changing a score requires that evidence, not merely a lower price. Public disclosures may not supply private bank detail, but material funded execution can still be triangulated from reconciled cash flows, quantified collections, debt and monitoring statements. If public evidence cannot establish it, keep the relevant score NS instead of demanding impossible precision or treating missing daily data alone as distress.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: unresolved special-situation / speculative execution watchlist; not a verified quality compounder and not eligible for numerical BQS/GQS/IAS ranking. G 1 Conditional, G 2 Hold, G 3 Hold, G 4 Conditional. BQS NS, GQS NS and IAS NS follow exact missing-input rules; the GQS cap 5 remains an explicit constraint, not a substitute point. CAP/REV missingness does not mean zero growth or zero returns, and it is not silently imputed to a peer average. The observed cash weakness is independently scoreable despite uncertainty about what a fuller reconciliation may show.

Action category: defer a fresh investment conclusion until reliability and funding cures are available. The repair-case₹100 approximately 15% hurdle threshold is conditional on favorable recovery timing, eligible IPO liquidity and modeled execution, not an actionable limit order or fair-value certificate. A cheaper quote cannot solve a material accounting gap; conversely the current high multiple amplifies the importance of proving cash and durable economics. No personal holding is assumed and no buy/sell instruction is issued. If the user later supplies an actual position or risk budget, liquidity and taxes must be recalculated rather than treating₹5 lakh as suitable. At this quoteone lot costs₹349,440 andtwo exceed₹500,000; the reference budget cannot be deployed precisely. Keep the company on the SME research page in the same v 3 format as mainboard research, without commingling its lot/trading constraints with mainboard implementation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Sources are official exchange or issuer-hosted primary filings, with downloaded byte hashes, dates, page locators and an explicit retention policy. The complete annual reports, prospectus financial statements and audit annexures were reviewed. September publication is not a new audit date: both FY26 versions are signed 28 May. The July reply is a format/segment clarification, not a cure of asset evidence. Source identifiers in every section and factor map to the ledger below. Market inputs retain all 60 official dates, internal trading date checks, exact ISIN/symbol matches, original archive hashes, OHLC, volume and turnover; absent sessions are not silently zero-filled. Security master lot/share count is dated 19 October. No post 20 Oct announcement is used.

Formula dictionary: operating EBIT equals revenue minus material, expensed subcontract, employee, other operating cost and DA; normalized EBIT additionally expenses capitalized R&D and adds back the identified IPO charge. NOPAT uses 25.17% analyst tax. Reported FCF=CFO−reported cash capex. Average DSO=(opening AR+closing AR)/2 divided by annual revenue times fiscal days; unbilled days is a separate closing balance metric. Incremental ROIC=change in normalized NOPAT/change in consistently defined operating IC, with explicit windows and no absent FY21 base invented. Model ONWC separates oldduebalances paidonce; cash floor failures including before entry nullnon-rescue terminal equity, returns and hurdle prices. Exact 1826-day ownership return=(exit per-share value/entry price)^(365.25/1826)−1, no dividends assumed. Hurdle entry price=terminal per-share value/(1+hurdle)^(1826/365.25). Hypothetical rescue uses whole new shares, grossproceeds,2% fee, net cash and diluted ownership, never theordinary denominator.

Open questions are substantive: auditor-version reconciliation; date and cash proof of related repayment; confirmation/collection ageing of billed and unbilled assets; loan-versus-advance classification; IPO expense/utilization and deposit restrictions; cash/noncash ROU presentation; product first sale and amortization; minimum utilization/termination/payment clauses of large contracts; andnetmargins afterstaffing, royalty, R&D, warranty andworking capital. Neither a favorable company statement nor a hostile inference fills these gaps. The model assumptions are fully retained alongside derivedrows, and all ordinary outputs remainnull while material G 2/G 3 issues persist.

The following reconciliation register is deliberately not polished away. Original PDFs, OCR, HTML, images, personal PANs/shareholderlists and transfer credentials are excluded from the private backups. Both compact and full archives retain the source-safe inputs and builders required to reconstruct every derived output fromabsence; source hashes do not replace the need to revisit a primarysource when updating facts. This dossier is research, not a statement of fraud, default or a personal investment recommendation.

summary:
Optivalue Tek is a small IT integration, consulting and staffing business attempting a more capital-intensive software, licensed anti-drone and hardware expansion. Reported FY26 revenue of₹90.74 crore and several large announced contracts create a plausible growth story; they do not yet establish a cash-generating compounder. The decisive risk is the unreconciled audit-evidence conflict over₹59.87 crore receivables and approximately₹14 crore unbilled revenue, compounded by negative operating cash and object-restricted IPO funds. Preserve the favorable facts: related advances are stated to have been repaid with interest, annual audit/IFC opinions are unmodified, and the annual audit describes alternative collection checks. Those facts do not quantify a cure.

At the verified 19 October close₹218.40, market capitalization is₹511.30 crore. Ordinary expected return, fair entry price and all three composite scores are NS, with G 2/G 3 Hold and no numerical ranking. This is an unresolved special-situation / execution watchlist, not a verified compounder or a fresh-entry recommendation. Even an explicitly optimistic, funded early-repayment repair model gives -1.6% annualized return at the quoted price and a conditional 15% hurdle price₹100.03; that number is not a buying recommendation while reliability and current funding remain unknown. Evidence of collected opening balances, authorized recoveries, usable funding and profitable product delivery would matter more than another headline order.
